surface_mechanism_description: The reduction process involves the nucleation and growth of nuclei, with the rate of reduction being proportional to the rate coefficient and the gas-phase hydrogen concentration. The model assumes instantaneous nucleation and two-dimensional nuclei growth, with the reduction advancing as growing centers on the surface of the supported catalyst.
evidence: The model of two-dimensional nuclei growth, alongside the concept of extended reduction degree, gives a good description of the experimental results. The nucleation parameters obtained a multiplicity of values so that the nucleation became instantaneous and virtually complete before the nuclei growth started. The two-dimensional growth of converting centers is highly acceptable for the supported well-dispersed catalyst with Cr6+ on the surface.
